newsitem.title: USA: Stericycle acquires Waste Management unit.
newsitem.headline: Stericycle acquires Waste Management unit.

text.p: Stericycle Inc on Monday said it acquired the majority of Waste Management Inc's medical waste business for $11 million in cash and notes.
"We expect the acquisition to increase our annual revenues by more than $12 million, or 50 percent," said Stericycle Chief Executive Mark Miller.
Stericycle, which went public in August, expects about $24 million in revenues for the year ending December 31, 1996.
Stericycle said it acquired from Waste Management the majority of its medical waste business, excluding certain treatment assets in Wisconsin.
Stericycle paid $5.5 million in cash and delivered a note for $5.5 million, it said.

"This is the fifth acquisition the company has made in 1996 and the first acquisition since the company's initial public offering in August, in which it raised more than $25 million," said Stericycle, which sells services for medical waste collection, transportation, treatment, disposal, reduction and resource recovery.

"From a strategic perspective, this acquisition accelerates our growth potential by extending our geographic reach from about 27 percent of the U.S. population to potentially more than 45 percent of the U.S. population. Expanded service regions include the mid-Atlantic, Ohio Valley, the Southwest and Mountain regions," said chief executive Mark Miller.

"An additional benefit of the acquisition will be a working relationship with Waste Management, providing for future cooperative marketing activities and expanded potential access to Waste Management sites," the company said.
